course: This course is an advanced Ottoman readings course and every class is basically organised in three phases. First phase is the transcription of the text into Latin script. Second phase is the grammatical analysis and the last phase is the translation of the text into modern Turkish. Hence, we learn not only reading but also understanding the Ottoman texts. Reading is an important skill yet does not necessarily bring about understanding automatically. In this way, the course was extremely useful compared to other Ottoman reading courses I took elsewhere.

Professor Ergenc is simply an outstanding teacher and instructor. He is very knowledgable and experienced. His main area of specialisation is the urban history of the Ottoman Empire. Nevertheless his detailed knowledge of the Ottoman Empire extends well beyond that and covers many broad themes and topics as the history of the institutions, history of statecraft and history of social movements, to give a few examples. He is also very knowledgable in historical method and the approaches of various social sciences, such as anthropology and sociology, towards the study of history. His classes are always vivid and encourage students to use their creativities and imaginations to solve various historical problems. That does not mean that he is devoid of methodology though. He attaches great importance to historical methodology, in particular philology and palaeography, and successfully combines this rigid scientific method with creative imagination to look for answers in history. Due to his long and extensive experience in academia, he is very patient and transfers his knowledge to his students skilfully. He is the padishah of Ottoman Studies. I feel privileged to be his student.

course: Bu dersi alacak arkadaşlar bunu sıradan bir ileri seviye Osmanlıca dersi gibi düşünmesinler. Hem tarih hem edebiyat bölümlerinde ileri seviye Osmanlıca derslerinde genellikle farklı yazı tipleri hızlıca okunur ve geçilir. Bu derste ise önce bir belge okunuyor, sonra metnin gramatikal analizi yapılıyor, daha sonra ise metin günümüz diline çevriliyor ve bir tarih çalışmasında bunun nasıl kullanılabileceği üzerine konuşuluyor. Bu aşamaların her biri çok önemli ama bence en önemlisi cümle analizi çünkü Osmanlıca metinlerin asıl zorluğu Farsça ve Arapça kelimelerin çokluğu değil cümle yapısının bugüne göre çok daha uzun ve karmaşık olması. Normalde bir tarihçi bu tarz belgeleri uzun yıllar arşiv deneyimi edindikten sonra rahatlıkla anlamaya başlar. Bu dersle yıllar içinde kazanılacak bu deneyim sistemli bir şekilde öğrenciye kazandırılmış oluyor.

The instructor has a special ability to teach Ottoman history and Ottoman Turkish, which basically originates from his background and long teaching experience in the Ottoman field. Both in understanding Ottoman literature and in history, he has broadened our vision. His teaching approach to history and literature reading is based on his amazing pedagogical skills, which are based on prompting the students to absorb the information in intermittent phases. Which makes his teaching offering permanent and durable knowledge. This approach not only helps us to absorb and acquire the information in the long run, but also helps us to internalize the information to use it in history writing, because knowledge without internalized or thoroughly acquired cannot be used in a practical need. What Özer Hoca is doing is making the students acquire the knowledge and use in history craftsmanship. Therefore, his classes offer more than a paleography lesson but also teach historiography and history craftsmanship.
course: Kolay bir ders değil yapısı itibariyle. Osmanlıca hususunda en büyük gelişimi sağlayabileceğimiz ders.

The lessons in the class basically consist of three phases that each student must proceed through one by one when a new paper is assigned.  Firstly, the reading phase, which basically requires being able to read the paper(and transcribe). In this phase, the hoca makes students recite the paper and have it read on the board. This was easy for our case as we had no hardship in Ottoman Turkish reading. The second phase, however, was at least for my case, the most toilsome and demanding phase. As one 'orta-zaman' Ottoman Turkish phrase might have seven different verbs in one sentence, and narrate the events with various subordinate clauses, understanding Ottoman Turkish becomes very challenging for a modern Turkish reader. Therefore, the second phase of the lesson is exactly for resolving this problem. In this phase, students are taught how to disintegrate the sentences on the paper, which is written in 'orta-zaman' Turkish. With a long, complex, and intricate inşa' style, which makes the understanding of Ottoman texts a great challenge for many historians. This course exactly challenges this difficulty by teaching students how to disintegrate these complex, intricate, and challenging Ottoman phrases into their components, subordinate clauses, etc. I might well say that Özer Hoca's method helped us to understand Ottoman literature in depth. And lastly, the third phase is offering employment of the paper as a historical source in the hands of a historian. The students are assigned to use the source and deduce historical knowledge from just using the paper with a heuristic approach. After fulfilling the second part, this phase becomes easy and helps history students to increase their history craftsmanship. All in all, the course was highly informative and inspirational for future historians. Thank you, Bilkent.
